content.introduction: This week's economic calendar highlights a steady stream of labor market data leading up to the highly anticipated Jobs Friday report. On Tuesday, November 3, the Job Openings & Labor Turnover Survey and Factory Orders are scheduled. On Wednesday, November 4, the ADP National Employment Report is due, focusing on private sector job changes. The sources also mention the Richmond Fed Manufacturing Shipments Index and Richmond Fed Services Revenues Index on Thursday, November 5. Additionally, the week includes the release of Initial Jobless Claims and Continuing Jobless Claims on Friday, November 6. These reports will provide insights into the labor market and economic conditions leading up to the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
body:
"We estimate that nonfarm payroll employment grew 50,000 in October, following gains in August (+133,000) and September (+29,000)," writes Barclays Chief U.S. Economist Marc Giannoni in a preview of incoming Jobs Friday data.

According to Giannoni's math, his headline forecast would work out to a three-month moving average of 71,000 new jobs, ahead of the 28,000 pace for the three months through July. [...] Tuesday (11/3)

A steady stream of labor market data builds toward Jobs Friday on this week's economic calendar.

[...] The economist forecast an unemployment rate of 4.1% for October, down from 4.2% for September. He expects unemployment to trend lower and job gains to somewhat exceed breakeven pace through 2026.

A combination of 50,000 new jobs and slightly lower joblessness in October "would keep an FOMC hike in play for the December meeting, as it continues to assess data developments," Giannoni concludes.
